question: Cognizant GenC technical interview (Java and OOP, described as "very important"): **compare abstract classes and interfaces. Can an abstract class have a constructor? Can you create an object of an abstract class? When do you use each?** Related questions in the same interviews: overloading versus overriding and why encapsulation is used.
lookingFor: Accurate comparison, including modern Java features (default methods).
Correct answers to the constructor and instantiation questions.
Judgement on when to choose each.
followUps: Why can't an interface have a constructor?
What problem do default methods solve, and what is the diamond problem with them?
Can an abstract class have no abstract methods?
What is the difference between method overloading and overriding?
